title: Amherst to launch Community Heart & Soul initiative with community dinner on Nov. 6 - West Massachusetts News

Government
Amherst to launch Community Heart & Soul initiative with community dinner on Nov. 6
The Town of Amherst will introduce its new Community Heart & Soul initiative with a public dinner event on November 6 at Bangs Community Center. Organizers say this program aims to foster collaboration among residents around shared values for shaping Amherst’s future.
The Town of Amherst announced on Oct. 28 the launch of its new Community Heart & Soul initiative, beginning with a community dinner scheduled for Friday, November 6 from 5:00 to 7:00 pm at the Bangs Community Center. The event is open to all residents and will feature food from local businesses, opportunities to connect with neighbors, and information about the initiative.
Community Heart & Soul invites members of Amherst to reflect on what they value most about their town, envision its future, and collaborate on how to achieve shared goals. The program builds upon Amherst’s ongoing efforts in equity, inclusion, and community engagement, including work by the Community Safety Working Group and a recent Liberatory Visioning process led by Dr. Barbara Love.
“Amherst residents have already spoken up, telling the Town what they need, what they envision, and what changes they believe are necessary,” said Bonnie Isman, Community Heart & Soul Core Team Member, League of Women Voters Member, and Former Jones Library Director. “Now, Amherst Community Heart & Soul will bring everyone together to collaborate on achieving these goals and building the Amherst we want to see.”
Pamela Nolan Young, Director of the Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Department, said: “The aim of this project is to bring Amherst community members, organizations, and businesses together to collectively solve previously identified concerns. It is about forming community, coalition building, and co-creation. The DEI Department is currently helping launch this initiative but ultimately it will be resident-led and operate independently of town government.”
The initiative is supported by a $10,000 Community Heart & Soul Seed Grant awarded to Amherst. According to organizers in the announcement article published by the Town of Amherst website itself (https://www.amherstma.gov/m/newsflash/Home/Detail/4016), Community Heart & Soul has been developed over more than a decade in partnership with over 140 small cities and towns across America as a process for engaging communities in shaping their futures.
JuPong Lin said: “Amherst is a Town that embraces a diverse range of perspectives. And like any small town many residents have not felt included in town decisions... Nationwide we’re facing the worst divisiveness we’ve ever seen. Community Heart & Soul hopefully provides an opportunity to gather and share our stories and work through our differences together.” Tonika Reed-Prempeh added that fostering positive coalition building through events such as storytelling would help create "a lasting network of mutual support." Registration for one of two seatings at either 5 pm or 6 pm is required; childcare will be available.
